activism.direction_note: Reconstructed on a comparable scale; the raw Estimate column mixes percent and decimal across studies.

border.direction_note: Raw coefficient on the border dummy in a log-linear gravity model; the paper's headline reduction is a transform of it, not the raw value.

dst.direction_note: SIGN TRAP: the stored value is the impact on electricity CONSUMPTION, so NEGATIVE means savings and is the favourable direction (median -0.40). The abstract instead frames the headline as a positive magnitude, 'slight electricity savings: 0.34%'. Taking the sign at face value inverts the finding.

electricity.direction_note: Marshallian-equivalent price elasticity (the paper's Slutsky-converted effect_M), negative by convention. Pools short-, intermediate- and long-run estimates, which the paper analyses separately; condition on the run-length flags in the per-dataset file rather than pooling blind.

esg.direction_note: Points on the Bloomberg/LSEG ESG scale per percentage point of board gender diversity, not a percent change.

euro.direction_note: Raw gravity-model coefficient on the currency-union dummy; the headline trade effect is a transform of it.

forward.direction_note: The null of interest is a slope of 1, not 0. Testing against zero will mislead.

gasoline.direction_note: Long-run income elasticity only; see the dataset note for the short-run estimates. CAUTION on n_obs: it is the file's Observations column, which init.do weights by as sqrt(Observations), but 90 of 701 rows record 1, which is not a plausible sample size and may be a missing-value code. Filter before using n_obs as a precision instrument.

gasoline_price.direction_note: Negative by convention: demand falls as price rises.

habits.direction_note: Unitless, normally bounded by 0 (no habit) and 1 (full persistence).

house_prices.direction_note: Stored as a PROPORTION: house.do multiplies by 100 for the percentages the paper reports. Negative is the expected direction, higher policy rates lowering house prices. One row per impulse-response horizon, so rows within an IRF are not independent.

incentives.direction_note: Baseline measure. Cohen's d, the paper's robustness variant, is in the per-dataset file.

migrant.direction_note: Stored as a negative inverse elasticity; a sign flip and inversion are needed to read it as the substitution elasticity discussed in the paper. Verify before pooling.

price_puzzle.units: proportional change in the price level
price_puzzle.direction_note: Stored as a PROPORTION, not a percent: multiply by 100 to read as the paper does (median |effect| 0.002 = 0.2%, consistent with its reported 0.33% trough). Positive values are the puzzling price INCREASE after a monetary contraction; theory expects negative. One row per horizon.

reforms.direction_note: Computed here from the reported t-statistic and degrees of freedom, following the paper's own code.

scc.units: US dollars per tonne of carbon

size.direction_note: Raw size-return slopes: NEGATIVE means a larger conventional size premium, i.e. small firms outperforming. The abstract states that researchers prefer estimates showing 'a negative relation between size and returns'. 76% of stored effects are negative. Do not read positive as the premium.

skill.direction_note: Stored as inverse elasticities; inversion is needed to read them as the skill-substitution elasticity. Dropping this step reverses the finding.

trust.direction_note: Raw size-return slopes: more negative means a larger conventional size premium.

fdi.direction_note: Winsorised FDI spillover elasticity (e_w). No standard error exists in the file, so this dataset supports model averaging over study characteristics but not SE-based synthesis.

lags.direction_note: Transmission lag: months from the monetary shock to the trough of the price response (mon_bot). A duration, not a regression coefficient, so it has no sampling standard error.

substitution.direction_note: Elasticity of intertemporal substitution. Same 2,735 estimates as the eis dataset; this file adds country-level moderators.

spillovers._note: Units come from overrides.json for this literature; entry added so units.json covers all 39 pooled literatures rather than 38. Absence here previously read as 'no sign trap' when it actually meant 'not present'. Gap found by the Fable audit, 2026-08-04.
